parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is cohesive: it holds order and stock use cases, and all of them reach persistence through the domain repositories (OrderRepository, ProductRepository) and StockManager. There is no persistence bypass. However, a rule is duplicated. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase writes out its own list of valid statuses (`validStatuses`), a copy of the OrderStatus definition in the domain Order entity. The copy also appears to leave out 'cancelled', so it may already have drifted. The entity's own transitionTo method is the abstraction meant to govern status changes. Separately, the Order-to-OrderDto mapping is copied inline in four use cases instead of living in one shared mapper.

violations.message: The `validStatuses` array copies the OrderStatus status set from the domain Order entity and appears to leave out 'cancelled'. The entity's transitionTo should be the single place that checks status changes.

The private `mapToDto` holds the Order-to-OrderDto mapping. The same mapping is copied in CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStatusUseCase and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase instead of being one shared mapper.
`execute` builds the OrderDto with an inline copy of the Order-to-OrderDto mapping instead of using a shared mapper.
